column1: bosses, minibosses, and elites are immune to being moved or repositioned, and may be immune to certain ailments or affects

if a target has been hit with a chain lighting, it cannot be proc'ed by the same chain lighting (like, it cant bounce to A, B, then back to A), and the target cant be hit by another chain lighting until the 'shock' window is passed (we need a cooldown time from when a shock or chain lighting hit can hit the enemy again, maybe like .1 or .2 seconds)

when time is slowed or stopped from chrono passive, its because left thumb is off; which means right thumb can still turn the ship and abilities can be activated from the right side activated button (these all swap if the player has mirror setting on for their playability)

all actives need a duration if not listed, and a cooldown. each duration and cooldown can be very different;just because an ability takes multiple elements doesnt mean its 'bigger' per se, it could be powerful due to its frequency you can use it

for 2 and 3 guns, they player can attune multiple elements. all elements apply to all beams (keeps it simple, and fun). for something like gamma and cryo, the gamma would extend the range (not width) of the cryo shot.

lots of things are determined by distance, or radius. i think we have a radius 1, radius 2, and a radius 3, so that we arent calculating it out unique every time. so we anchor radius 1 as n units, radius 2 is always y units, radius 3 is z units. do the same for distances. this makes it easy across the board and visually. we can call it short, medium, large radius in tooltips with the unit count, but backend we call it radius_dist1, or something akin
bow is front of a ship, stern is the back of the ship
some abilities have charges. the cooldown begins once the first charge is expended, to replenish more charges.

for nomenclature, this may help with coding objects, but 'player' is referred to the players ship. 'user' refers to the person navigating the menu, not in ship control mode. unless we should have a better designation there? do we call 'player' the 'valrune' here? 'baddie' is anything the player can damage - any minion, elite, miniboss, boss, asteroid, debris, etc
debuffs and stacks always apply before the 'hit' of damage is taken; to both player and baddies

although variables will be declared in their own objects or functions, itd be more readable if we used same classifications of variables across the board so we can interpret easy as possible. ie, use r for radius units, dis for distance units, dur for duration, c for cooldown, s for stacks, dot for damage over time effect damage (like burn), dam for damage (ive used n in places but you can edit to dam), n for any number that i dont have a recurring classification for
cooldowns always begin once duration ends

need to come up with a list of debuffs that bosses are immune, bosses and minibosses are immune, and boss+miniboss+elite are immune; maybe we also could change the stack max that a boss can get? too complicated? i dont want a player to go to a boss and melt it. like, time slow stacks and stop on crit from chrono shouldnt affects bosses and minis, maybe still affects elites?

a regular set of variables for distance moved over time? like if an affect pushes, or pulls, it goes x distance in y frame. something like a short push from forge should be very small units, so the baddie still moves forward if its heading that way, but gets knocked back mini-bits as it tries. vs, a gravity pull which covers greater distance and needs to happen in y time, and may override a baddie's movement.

adding to the thought on 15, push and pull do not override movement, [gravity] is a status affect on the push or pull that does override movement. boss and miniboss should be immune to push, pull, and gravity; push and pull could be brief but speedy (like forge hits), or slow pull negative on a speed in a direction, like the first level passive of void
distance over time variable being mr for move rate? mr1 is super speedy?

i think we try to keep variable close to similar if possible, like the dis1 being the distance to the edge of r1's radius, dis2 matches r2, dis3 matches r3, then r_short for super short radius, and dis_short for super short distance (like a forge shot hit)

need to dictionary what we mean by fire, shot, projectile. sometimes i think im saying fire when meaning flame and sometimes meaning to shoot; same goes for projectile vs shot, im saying projectile a lot but mostly im meaning the shot (like, i say projectile but if theres 3 guns im actually referring to the entire shot, not a particular gun's shot)
attack disabled should not affect elites and up

baddies have actions, an action might be 'attack', where they shoot projectiles for duration, that action state stays units its duration ends; ie, baddie action is 'move' from point a to point b, in path type, gets there at s speed, then stops (move action ended). then it stays idle 3 seconds, then action shoot starts, 3 seconds into action shoot, action move starts and overlaps action move, until duration of each end.

a telegraph is a visual highlight of where a ship will move (white transparency highlight), or attack (red transparency highlight); the highlight is soft and extends the direction for duration, then has a deeper solid texture or glow before disappearing adn the action then ahppens

if an ability give bonus damage on a hit, and that hit crits, the crit only applies to the original unmodified damage (will help stop wicked power scaling math that might happen; ie, the bonus damage from forge's attunement - the regular damage number is preserved, so the crit applies to the original damage, then the forge bonus damage applies)

trying to avoid any most % increase or decrease functions, lets try to keep things as flat variables. this avoids wicked scaling. crit damage is one exception. highlight any that come up tho and we can decide what we want out of it. a 'crit' is not a source for any purposes that say a source causes something

damage needs types; damage can be mixed types just like elements can; damage types are the same name as the element 'cryo damage', 'forge damage', etc; burn is obvs plasma type; bonus damage from corrosive is caustic type, etc

no self-damage; mines, fire trails, etc, dont hurt the player. the baddies effects never hurt their own team; baddies immune to any baddie objects affects, bullets go thorugh as if friendly baddies not there
push and pull always have a source, so push is always away from source, pull is always towards source
burn duration is default 5 seconds

my single abilities may be too weak compared to the duals. duals and triples give variety, not more power. so a tier III single should be equal in power to a tier III dual; a tier III single or dual should be equal to a tier II triple, and a tier I triple equal to a tier II dual or single; the only exception id make for this, is a tier I single could be weaker than any other tier I, just because its early game and so cheap to attain; need to be creative on status ailment factoring, utility (like movement) factoring

how to math abilities: take a ship with no base upgrades with the node, and factor damage and health jump, then at node II and node III stage; then do it with half of everything upgraded (do 3 guns at half upgrade tho), node I II and III damage, then at fully max'ed upgraded (hitting max everythiing intended for ng+)

passives and actives should be equal power, its hard for me to math out damage or scaling with actives that are on cooldown vs passives that are continuous, so when you figure damage calculations - assume the raw damage number possible at ~2 minutes of play, and with an x amount of enemies, and for things that could affect enemies in range, estimate how many enemies could be hit by the thing out of all the enemies. will also need a single target estimate (how good is this as a boss killer) and a multi-target estimate (how good is it against mobs)

if a status effect woudl be applied again, it checks if the new apply would extend or shorten the duration (greeq fire); if it would shorten the duration, then it does not reapply; otherwise, it reapplies
ground just means the map or battle area, even tho its in space and techincally no 'ground' per se
maybe we need like, a burn and a burn+, shock or shock+, so we have factors of different status ailments

my chain lightning explanations are rough. when you go through this, have 'baddie_i' for initially hit baddie, then it can be, ie, chain lightning hits baddie_i, then jumps to the nearest baddie_1 within radius 1, then hits baddie_2 within radius_1 of baddie_1

i think we dont have an ability with more than a 1 min cooldown, so that it cna be used at least 2 times in most stages; many abilities could be 10, 15, 20, 30, etc as needed or makes sense for power scaling
somethings refer to basic attack or main attack, like, non-ability attack; i think we call these 'gun shots'? or something else?
thinking of keeping status effects anchored to the element; so, burn only comes from plasma, corrosion only from caustic, etc
when a stack is added, the cooldown for ALL stacks becomes the newest cooldown (avoid keeping track of lots of cooldown stacks)
